annotations.text:
COLOUR, AS YOU DECIDED

Pin fill = status. Green today, soft yellow ahead, grey done or past.
Each day's own hue shows up as the dot beside its header, not on the pins.
Opening a day dims every other day, which is what actually makes a cluster readable.

TRY IT

The first artboard is live. Tap a day header to open it, tap a stop to expand the actions, tap Visited to grey it out. Tap the grab handle to throw the sheet to full screen.

SOURCES, AS YOU DECIDED

Google My Maps, so we get a real KML endpoint with coordinates and genuine hourly sync. No scraping, no geocoding, nothing to break.

Gmail is out of v1. The spreadsheet is now a ONE-TIME import, not a sync - the screen on the right runs once, you fix what it got wrong, and then the Planner below owns the trip.

THE ANSWER TO YOUR SPREADSHEET QUESTION

You were right that parsing other people's layouts forever does not work. So this view IS the spreadsheet: days across, time down, drag cells around, the lodging row along the bottom. Everything your sheet does, except the cells know where they are on Earth.

Export CSV is in the top right so nobody feels trapped.

Three ways to shape the day list. A is what the app screens are built on, because it is what you described. B and C are here so you can see what you are giving up. They are sketches, not proposals - say the word and I will build one out properly.
